---

## Key structural points (Hansen)

1. **2:19–30 is not a conventional letter-close.** Travelogues display “the presence of apostolic authority and power”; emissaries + promise of personal visit back the letter’s imperatives.
2. **Timothy and Epaphroditus illustrate 2:4–8 / 2:5:** Timothy = genuine concern / not own interests; Epaphroditus = risk near death // Christ obedient unto death.
3. **3:1–21 is not an interpolated fragment** (contra Beare). Continuity via positive/negative exemplar pattern across the letter.
4. **3:1** = epistolary hesitation formula + transition (“further”), not farewell; “same things” = repeated command to **rejoice in the Lord**; “safeguard” = **stability/firmness**.
5. **3:2–3** negative triad (dogs, evildoers, mutilation/*katatomē*) vs true **circumcision/*peritomē***: Spirit-worship, boast in Christ, no confidence in flesh. Opponents = Judaizing teachers (potential threat, not yet embedded in Philippi).
6. **3:4–6** Paul’s résumé is ad hominem superiority in “flesh” then renounced; **faultless** = observable law-performance (not sinless; uses means of atonement), not a general soteriological principle that law-keeping perfects.
7. **3:7–11** second self-portrait: accounting loss/gain; salvation sketched as justification (v. 9) / sanctification-participation (v. 10) / glorification-resurrection (v. 11); strong parallel to Christ hymn 2:5–11; Hansen defends **faith *in* Christ** (objective genitive) and rejects pure NPP reading of “my own righteousness” as *only* national membership.

---

## Claims

### V. Recommendations of Christ-like Servants (2:19–30) — function

**E1.** Hansen (section open): After direct exhortation, Paul presents Timothy and Epaphroditus as “dynamic examples… who embody the Christ-like attitudes he has been encouraging.”  
- Quote: “Paul now presents the dynamic examples of two men, Timothy and Epaphroditus, who embody the Christ-like attitudes he has been encouraging his readers to have in their relationships with one another.”  
- Locus: slice open, “V. RECOMMENDATIONS…”

**E2.** Hansen rejects reading 2:19–30 as Paul *ending* the letter with conventional travel plans.  
- Quote: “But concluding his letter does not appear to be Paul’s purpose in this section. In fact, Paul’s travelogues do not primarily function as a conclusion to his letters.”  
- Locus: 2:19–30 intro

**E3.** Hansen: Pauline travelogues share (a) intention to send emissaries and (b) plan for personal visit; underlying purpose is display of apostolic authority/power.  
- Quote: “the underlying purpose of these travelogues is to display ‘the presence of apostolic authority and power - of which the travelogue in the narrow sense is only one element.’”  
- Locus: 2:19–30 intro (citing scholarship Hansen follows)

**E4.** Hansen: letter substitutes for presence; promise of visit and emissaries add weight so imperatives are implemented.  
- Quote: “Since the letter functioned as a substitute for Paul’s physical presence, Paul added weight to the apostolic authority of the letter by promising that he would visit the congregation soon in person…”  
- Locus: 2:19–30 intro

**E5.** Hansen links examples to prior imperatives/hymn: Timothy // 2:4; Epaphroditus // 2:7–8.  
- Quote: “By his genuine concern for the welfare of the Philippians in a time when everyone looks out for their own interests (2:20-21), Timothy illustrates the altruistic attitude Paul desired… (2:4). When Epaphroditus almost died because he risked his life… (2:30), he mirrored Christ, who took the very nature of a servant and was obedient unto death (2:7-8).”  
- Locus: 2:19–30 intro

**E6.** Hansen: Christ’s attitude (2:5) becomes tangible in contemporary servants.  
- Quote: “To have the same attitude of mind Christ Jesus had (2:5) seems intangible until that attitude is exhibited in contemporary servants of Christ.”  
- Locus: 2:19–30 intro

### A. Timothy (2:19–24)

**E7.** Lemma (TNIV as Hansen prints): hope to send Timothy soon; no one like him with genuine concern; everyone looks to own interests not those of Jesus Christ; Timothy proved as son with father in gospel work; send when Paul sees how things go; confident in the Lord he himself will come soon.  
- Locus: 2:19–24 block lemma

**E8.** Hansen on *elpizō* “I hope”: Greek implies confidence of a future event, not English-style uncertainty.  
- Quote: “Although the English word may connote a high degree of uncertainty, the Greek word implies confidence of a future event.”  
- Locus: 2:19

**E9.** Hansen: hope “in the Lord Jesus” = plans under Lord’s direction, submitted for approval, dependence for realization.  
- Quote: “his hope is in the Lord Jesus indicates that he makes his travel plans under the direction of the Lord Jesus, submits his plans to the Lord Jesus for approval, and depends upon the Lord Jesus for the realization of his plans.”  
- Locus: 2:19

**E10.** Hansen: Timothy’s sending delayed until Paul sees how things go (imprisonment/trial, 2:23), but “soon”; Paul envisions brief interval of improvement.  
- Quote: “Although Timothy’s departure was delayed until Paul could see how things would go for him in his personal situation, presumably in his imprisonment and upcoming trial (2:23), the delay would not be for long.”  
- Locus: 2:19, 2:23

**E11.** Hansen: positivity about future is from hope/confidence “in the Lord,” not sanguine temperament or news analysis; whether special revelation or simple trust “we cannot be sure.”  
- Quote: “Whether he means that he simply trusts in the goodness of the Lord or that he has received a special revelation from the Lord regarding his future, we cannot be sure.”  
- Locus: 2:19, 2:24

**E12.** Hansen: purpose of sending Timothy includes Paul being “cheered” by news of the church; *eupsucheō* (only here in NT) = heartened/glad/have courage.  
- Quote: “Used only here in the NT, the word cheered means ‘to be heartened, be glad, have courage.’”  
- Locus: 2:19

**E13.** Hansen: emphasis on impact of *church’s* condition on Paul presses them toward unity (2:2).  
- Quote: “This emphasis on his deep concern for the welfare of the church puts pressure on the church to cheer him up by following his directive to be one in spirit and of one mind (2:2).”  
- Locus: 2:19

**E14.** Hansen on *isopsychos* (“equal-soul”): not absolute uniqueness of Timothy but closeness to Paul — “no one else who is as equal to me as Timothy is.”  
- Quote: “points not to the absolute uniqueness of Timothy (there is no one equal to Timothy) but to the closeness of Timothy and Paul (there is no one else who is as equal to me as Timothy is).”  
- Locus: 2:20

**E15.** Hansen: “genuine” (*gnēsios*) evokes legitimate/true family member; cf. 1 Tim 1:2 “true son in the faith.”  
- Quote: “The adjectival form of this word genuine refers to ‘one who is considered a valid member of a family, legitimate, true.’”  
- Locus: 2:20

**E16.** Hansen distinguishes *merimnaō* anxiety (4:6 forbid) from Timothy’s genuine concern for welfare; body members should have concern for each other (1 Cor 12:25).  
- Quote: “Paul draws a line between obsessive anxiety and genuine concern… Caring for the needs of friends should not lead to anxiety; freedom from anxiety should not lead to a lack of concern for friends.”  
- Locus: 2:20

**E17.** Hansen on “everyone looks out for their own interests” (2:21): preferred generous reading = certain coworkers unwilling to go to Philippi, not total condemnation of all Christians; links to 1:15–17 envious preachers; may also have some Philippians in view given 2:3–4.  
- Quote: “A generous interpretation takes everyone as a reference to certain coworkers who should have been available but were unwilling to be sent by Paul to Philippi because they were preoccupied with their own interests.” … “In the light of his exhortations to the believers in Philippi, he has some of them in mind when he makes his judgment of everyone.”  
- Locus: 2:21

**E18.** Hansen: second reason for sending Timothy = Philippians’ knowledge that he “has proved himself” (test with reference to result); proven character via perseverance in suffering (Rom 5:3–4) and faithful gospel service (2 Cor 9:13).  
- Quote: “refers to ‘the experience of going through a test with special reference to the result.’”  
- Locus: 2:22

**E19.** Hansen: “as a son with his father he has served with me” features loyalty and humility; Greco-Roman/Jewish filial honor; Timothy’s words will represent Paul’s heart/mind; cf. 1 Cor 4:17.  
- Quote: “Timothy’s loyalty to Paul was not the loyalty of a cold professional, but the intimate loyalty of a son to his father.”  
- Locus: 2:22

**E20.** Hansen stresses Pauline shift: not “served *me*” but “served *with me* in the work of the gospel”; gospel is final authority; both “servants of Christ Jesus (1:1).”  
- Quote: “in a surprising, yet totally Pauline shift of direction, Paul does not say that Timothy served me, but that he served with me in the work of the gospel. The gospel was the final authority for Paul as well as for Timothy.”  
- Locus: 2:22

**E21.** Hansen: “work of the gospel” = evangelism *and* guiding community to live worthy of the gospel (1:27); “active love is the obedience of the confession of the Gospel” (Hansen quoting/paraphrasing line of thought he affirms).  
- Quote: “the work of the gospel provides not only the foundation for the community but also the continuing direction for community life.”  
- Locus: 2:22

**E22.** Hansen: Timothy’s humility as son/slave mirrors Christ hymn language so readers see Timothy has “the same attitude of mind Christ Jesus had (2:5).”  
- Quote: “In Paul’s recommendation of Timothy, he uses the same language as the hymn to Christ so that his readers will know that Timothy has the same attitude of mind Christ Jesus had (2:5).”  
- Locus: 2:22

**E23.** Hansen on 2:23 delay: “how things go with me” is vague; common speculation = trial outcome; alternatives = need for Timothy’s companionship, or conflicts with 1:15–17 preachers; **admits ignorance**.  
- Quote: “Reasonable hypotheses can be formulated to fill in the gaps left by Paul’s ambiguous note, but in the end we must admit our ignorance.”  
- Locus: 2:23

**E24.** Hansen: clear timing point = after seeing how things go, Timothy sent “at once.”  
- Quote: “The only clear point in his note about the timing of Timothy’s visit is that after he saw how things would go for him, he would send Timothy to Philippi ‘at once.’”  
- Locus: 2:23

**E25.** Hansen on 2:24: “I myself” stresses no one fully replaces Paul; personal presence shows commitment and seriousness of church crisis; unity fully restored only by his presence; letter + agents promote restoration meanwhile.  
- Quote: “Evidently, Paul believes that true unity in the church can be fully restored only by his own personal presence.”  
- Locus: 2:24

**E26.** Hansen: “I am confident” (*pepoitha*) same high certainty as 1:25 (remain alive) and 1:6 (God will complete the work).  
- Quote: “We can see the high level of certainty expressed by this verb when we note that Paul uses the same verb I am confident to express his settled conviction that God will complete the work that he began in the Philippian community (1:6).”  
- Locus: 2:24

**E27.** Hansen on “in the Lord”: given strong certainty, prefers that Lord has approved or inspired the plans (not mere “if the Lord wills” soft condition alone).  
- Quote: “Given Paul’s strong sense of certainty about his future plans, his expression in the Lord appears to mean that Paul is sure that the Lord has already given his stamp of approval on these plans or was in fact the original source of inspiration for these plans.”  
- Locus: 2:24

**E28.** Hansen notes dating puzzle: Rome after Romans 15:17–24 east-work “finished” vs Philippi visit; Paul changed plans (2 Cor 1); Caesarea or Ephesus provenance fits more easily.  
- Quote: “If Paul wrote this letter from prison in Rome after writing his letter to Rome, a trip back east to Philippi would seem to be in conflict with his strong statement in Romans 15:17-24…”  
- Locus: 2:24 (historical footnote in argument)

### B. Epaphroditus (2:25–30)

**E29.** Lemma: necessary to send Epaphroditus — brother, co-worker, fellow soldier; their messenger/care for needs; longs/distressed re illness report; ill, almost died; God mercy on him and Paul (sorrow upon sorrow); eager to send so they glad and Paul less anxiety; welcome with great joy and honor such people; almost died for work of Christ; risked life to make up help they could not give.  
- Locus: 2:25–30 lemma

**E30.** Hansen: Epaphroditus likely letter-bearer returning home; two stated reasons for sending: *his* longing (v. 26) and *their* joy at seeing him (v. 28); twice almost died (vv. 27, 30).  
- Quote: “The first reason is Epaphroditus’s need: for he longs for all of you (v. 26); the second reason is the Philippians’ need: so that when you see him again you may be glad (v. 28).”  
- Locus: 2:25–30 intro

**E31.** Hansen: near-death risk mirrors Christ (2:5, 7–8); though named for a Greek goddess, “he had the character of Christ.”  
- Quote: “Although Epaphroditus bore the name of a Greek goddess, he had the character of Christ, who took the form of a servant and was obedient to death (2:7-8).”  
- Locus: 2:25–30 intro

**E32.** Hansen entertains then softens “read between lines” motives: (a) assure church illness was real / mission not abandoned — “golden bridge for his retreat”; (b) forestall criticism for sending Epaphroditus not Timothy. Prefers face-value affection.  
- Quote: “Thus rather than read ulterior motives into words of affection we should take them at face value.”  
- Locus: 2:25–30 intro / after

**E33.** Hansen: “it is necessary” first in sentence contrasts delayed “soon” of Timothy/Paul with **immediate** send of Epaphroditus.  
- Quote: “But Paul thought it necessary to send Epaphroditus home immediately, without delay. The word necessary indicates that urgent, pressing needs forced or required him to send Epaphroditus home without delay.”  
- Locus: 2:25

**E34.** Hansen lists **five titles**: my brother, co-worker, fellow soldier; your messenger (*apostolos*); servant/leitourgos to Paul’s need.  
- Quote: “Paul honors him by giving him five titles: my brother, co-worker and fellow soldier, who is also your messenger, whom you sent to take care of my needs.”  
- Locus: 2:25

**E35.** Hansen: “my brother” with possessive = affectionate commitment, not bare Christian label; cf. sorrow upon sorrow if death (v. 27).  
- Quote: “Paul’s use of the possessive personal pronoun (my) to modify the first three titles for Epaphroditus emphasizes their affectionate relationship.”  
- Locus: 2:25

**E36.** Hansen: co-worker = inner circle for gospel advance; “work of Christ” here = help as church’s agent (v. 30); co-worker not unconditional equality; ultimately “God’s co-workers” (1 Cor 3:9).  
- Quote: “The term co-worker does not connote unconditional equality with Paul.”  
- Locus: 2:25

**E37.** Hansen: fellow soldier — work of Christ leads to warfare/suffering (1:29); Epaphroditus likely with Paul in prison.  
- Quote: “In Paul’s experience and theology, the work of Christ leads inevitably into warfare and suffering on behalf of Christ (1:29).”  
- Locus: 2:25

**E38.** Hansen on *apostolos*: not foundation-apostle status of Twelve/Paul, but church messenger (cf. 2 Cor 8:23) “without extraordinary status.”  
- Quote: “Paul is not using the word apostle with the special sense applied only to the ‘foundation-laying preachers of the gospel…’ … there were also ‘messengers of the churches’… in the general sense of ‘messengers without extraordinary status.’”  
- Locus: 2:25

**E39.** Hansen on servant/*leitourgos*: cultic/admin service or personal aide; Epaphroditus = personal assistant; needs include gifts (4:18) but **not limited to money** — “care for Paul in every way possible.”  
- Quote: “Surely, this service included but was not limited to financial support.”  
- Locus: 2:25 (with forward ref to 4:18)

**E40.** Hansen rejects pathologizing Epaphroditus’s longing/distress (homesickness, “nervous disorder,” unmanly emotion): same *epipotheō* as Paul (1:8); *adēmoneō* same word as Jesus in Gethsemane — not immaturity.  
- Quote: “Such negative interpretations are not warranted by Paul’s language here.” … “Paul in no way disapproves of the emotions of his brother, co-worker and fellow soldier.”  
- Locus: 2:26

**E41.** Hansen: why distress because they *heard* he was ill remains ambiguous (their distress vs fear of mission-failure judgment); “no evidence to confirm” conjectures.  
- Quote: “The ambiguity of this text gives rise to many conjectures, but offers no evidence to confirm any of them.”  
- Locus: 2:26

**E42.** Hansen: “Indeed he was ill, and almost died” — report understated seriousness; near death; no medical diagnosis.  
- Quote: “Apparently, Paul felt that the report that he was ill minimized the seriousness of the illness.”  
- Locus: 2:27

**E43.** Hansen: repetition of death (vv. 27, 30) echoes Christ hymn 2:8; suffering opportunity to reflect 2:5.  
- Quote: “The repetition of the word death in the story of Epaphroditus emphasizes the parallel to the narrative of Christ, who was obedient to death - even death on a cross! (2:8).”  
- Locus: 2:27

**E44.** Hansen: recovery attributed solely to God’s mercy (“Near death! But God!”); human prayer/recovery details obscured; encourages prayer *and* dependence on mercy whether recovery occurs or not.  
- Quote: “All human actions are obscured from view. Only God’s merciful action is seen. God had mercy on him.”  
- Locus: 2:27

**E45.** Hansen: mercy also on Paul “to spare me sorrow upon sorrow”; joy in letter is not Stoic apathy; sorrow is real for one whose motto is “to live is Christ.”  
- Quote: “Paul’s joy ‘has nothing to do with stoic apathy.’ Rejoicing in the Lord does not mean denying the reality of sorrow…”  
- Locus: 2:27

**E46.** Hansen: first sorrow’s cause unspecified (illness, imprisonment, rivals all guesses); admission of sorrow is **not** confession of sin; sorrow God-given/Christ-like especially before death as “last enemy” (1 Cor 15:26).  
- Quote: “But Paul’s admission of sorrow is not a confession of sin. The emotion of sorrow is a God-given, Christ-like emotion, especially in the face of death…”  
- Locus: 2:27

**E47.** Hansen on 2:28: “all the more eager” may imply plan change — original expectation stay until trial; illness trauma → send home sooner.  
- Quote: “the original expectation of the church and Paul may have been for Epaphroditus to stay with Paul indefinitely or at least until the outcome of his trial, but as a result of the trauma of his illness and relief at his recovery, Paul decided to send him home sooner than expected.”  
- Locus: 2:28

**E48.** Hansen: their “gladness/rejoice” is God-centered worship for mercy, not mere happiness; “less anxiety/sorrow” comparative — Paul does not expect freedom from all sorrow.  
- Quote: “His prescription for joy does not include the removal of all sorrow but such a focus on presence of the Lord within the experience of sorrow that rejoicing in the Lord becomes the predominant theme of life.”  
- Locus: 2:28

**E49.** Hansen on 2:29: command to welcome with great joy and honor; theories of hostile church critical of Epaphroditus “unconfirmed”; welcome “in the Lord” = belonging to saints; honor to such people is honor to Christ they reflect.  
- Quote: “Since Paul draws such close parallels between Epaphroditus and Christ, the honor given to such people as Epaphroditus is really honor given to Christ since such people reflect Christ.”  
- Locus: 2:29

**E50.** Hansen on 2:30: “work of Christ” ultimately Christ’s commission behind church and Paul; verbal parallel near death // obedient unto death.  
- Quote: “Epaphroditus came near to death//Christ was obedient unto death.”  
- Locus: 2:30

**E51.** Hansen **rejects** gambling wordplay (Epaphroditus / Aphrodite / dice invocation) for “risked”: verb = expose to danger; lexica lack gambling refs; thin evidence. Prefers echo of Mark 8:35 lose life for gospel.  
- Quote: “As fascinating as this interpretation is, however, it rests on thin evidence. The verb means to ‘expose to danger, risk.’”  
- Locus: 2:30

**E52.** Hansen on “make up for the help you yourselves could not give” / “supply your lack of service”: **not a rebuke**; *leitourgia* = sacred/priestly service; cf. 2:17 drink offering; **fragrant offering imagery at 4:18** (Hansen cites as complementary language for gifts). “Lack” = whole church’s personal absence; one messenger fills gap for many.  
- Quote: “At first glance this phrase may look like a rebuke for lack of service. But in fact Paul’s words communicate deep gratitude for the church and for their messenger, Epaphroditus.” … “When Paul refers to your lack (hymon hysterema) of service to me, he is not criticizing them, but simply recognizing the fact of their personal absence.”  
- Locus: 2:30 (fragrant offering: Hansen’s forward cross-ref to 4:18 within this paragraph)

**E53.** Hansen closes unit: friends’ portraits extend imperative of 2:5 — ordinary people sacrificial service as Christ.  
- Quote: “In this way his friends become an extension of his imperative to have the same attitude of mind Christ Jesus had (2:5).”  
- Locus: end of 2:25–30

### VI. Disclosures of Personal Experience (3:1–21) — chapter frame (within slice)

**E54.** Hansen: ch. 3 turns inward — conversion contrast Pharisee persecutor vs quest to know Christ; emotions of longing and tears for enemies of the cross; theology of justification/sanctification/glorification via experience; Christ center of Paul’s theology.  
- Quote: “In other words, Paul explains the whole process of salvation - justification, sanctification, and glorification - in terms of his own personal experience. All of his experience is centered in Christ.”  
- Locus: VI intro (3:1–21)

**E55.** Hansen lists landmines: identity of opponents; interpolation?; how Paul “faultless”?; *faith in Christ* vs faithfulness of Christ.  
- Quote: “Does the phrase faith in Christ mean the faithfulness of Christ or the faith of believers in Christ?”  
- Locus: VI intro

---

### A. Boasting in Privileges (3:1–6)

**E56.** Lemma 3:1–6: further/rejoice in Lord; same things no trouble, safeguard; watch dogs/evildoers/mutilators; we the circumcision — serve by Spirit, boast in Christ Jesus, no confidence in flesh; Paul’s greater flesh confidence; résumé (eighth day, Israel, Benjamin, Hebrew of Hebrews, Pharisee, zeal persecuting church, righteousness based on law faultless).  
- Locus: 3:1–6 lemma

**E57.** Hansen reports abruptness problem: “finally” sounds like conclusion then curse on dogs; if 3:2–21 cut, smooth 3:1→4:1.  
- Quote: “If 3:2-21 were cut out, there would be a smooth transition from 3:1 to 4:1.”  
- Locus: 3:1–6 intro

**E58.** Hansen records Beare interpolation hypothesis (3:1–21 fragment from another letter found at Philippi) and **rejects need for “radical surgery”**; many continuities; author’s right to change direction.  
- Quote: “The need for the proposed radical surgery of cutting out this section as ‘an interpolated fragment’ becomes less urgent when we see how well it fits within the unity of the entire letter.”  
- Locus: 3:1–6 intro

**E59.** Hansen on 3:1: “epistolary hesitation formula” — *graphō* + “trouble” better “cause of hesitation/reluctance” + negative; “I do not hesitate to write these things to you again”; expression of friendship.  
- Quote: “By using this conventional form, Paul is saying, ‘To write the same things to you is not a cause of hesitation for me’ or ‘I do not hesitate to write these things to you again.’”  
- Locus: 3:1

**E60.** Hansen: nearest referent of “same things” = command **rejoice in the Lord** (echoes 2:17–18, 29; later 4:4); friendship shares joys/sorrows; Lord = source/object/sphere of joy; corporate joy.  
- Quote: “The nearest reference point for the same things in the immediate context is the command: rejoice in the Lord!”  
- Locus: 3:1

**E61.** Hansen rejects “rejoice” = “farewell” here; *to loipon* (“further/finally”) marks remaining matter / transition, not necessarily letter end; here further inference from 2:29 welcome/honor → general rejoice.  
- Quote: “In the present context, this term works well as a marker for an additional command that flows inferentially out of the two previous commands: Welcome him in the Lord with great joy, and honor people like him (2:29); Further... rejoice in the Lord! (3:1).”  
- Locus: 3:1

**E62.** Hansen on “safeguard”: if “same things” = rejoice, adjective better **stability/firmness** than mere safety against dogs (though that third sense possible); links to stand firm (1:27; 4:1); joy strengthens in sacrifice/sorrow.  
- Quote: “To write the same things to you again, to repeat his imperatives to rejoice, is not a cause of hesitation for Paul and is a basis of stability for them.”  
- Locus: 3:1

**E63.** Hansen: 3:2 three warnings fit letter’s positive/negative exemplar pattern (welcome/honor/rejoice vs watch dogs/evildoers/mutilators); recurrence allays interpolation suspicion.  
- Quote: “The recurrence of this positive /negative pattern allays suspicion that an unrelated fragment from another letter has been inserted here…”  
- Locus: 3:2

**E64.** Hansen: *blepete* with dangerous objects = urgent warning, not calm academic observation of alternatives.  
- Quote: “Paul is not calmly advising his readers to do some academic analysis of possible alternatives; he is urgently warning them to watch out for harmful adversaries.”  
- Locus: 3:2

**E65.** Hansen identifies opponents as **Jewish-Christian / Judaizing**: exalt circumcision and Jewish credentials; turn tables by calling them names they used for outsiders (dogs, evildoers).  
- Quote: “Although they were posing as Christian teachers, they placed their emphasis on belonging to the Jewish people.” … “In this satirical twist, Paul gives them a bitter taste of their own poisonous prejudice.”  
- Locus: 3:2

**E66.** Hansen on location: not specific Philippi insiders; not merely past history; not only Rome rivals harming Paul; **potential visiting teachers** clear present danger (heat of Galatian-type conflict).  
- Quote: “The tentative conclusion… is that Paul is warning against false teachers who, though not yet in the church in Philippi, are nevertheless a clear and present danger.”  
- Locus: 3:2

**E67.** Hansen on “dogs”: despised scavengers in Jewish culture; Judaizers treated Gentile believers as unclean dogs; Paul redraws circle with Christ at center — holiness in Christ (1:1; 2:14–15); by despising purity in Christ, Judaizers become the dogs.  
- Quote: “By despising true purity in Christ, they put themselves in the place of dogs. Following this line of thought, Paul calls the Judaizers by their own favorite title for impure Gentiles: Watch out for those dogs!”  
- Locus: 3:2

**E68.** Hansen on “evildoers”: ironic reverse of self-image as law-workers/servants of righteousness; (1) law-emphasis → self-reliance obscuring need for salvation in Christ; (2) requiring circumcision/works harms by misleading to supplement faith with works.  
- Quote: “First, they are evildoers because their emphasis on the works of the law turns into a self-reliance that obscures the need for salvation in Christ. Second, they are evildoers because their work to convert Gentile Christians to Judaism… harms Christians by misleading them to supplement faith in Christ with works of the law.”  
- Locus: 3:2

**E69.** Hansen on “mutilators” / *katatomē* (“the mutilation”): sarcastic twist — circumcision as worthless as pagan mutilation if it replaces faith in Christ as basis of belonging; OT already required heart circumcision; applies to any ministers elevating ritual over faith/Spirit.  
- Quote: “circumcision, the sign of the Jewish covenant, has no more value than mutilation if it replaces faith in Christ as the basis of belonging to the people of God.”  
- Locus: 3:2

**E70.** Hansen on 3:3 “we… are the circumcision”: Gentile (and Jewish) believers already the covenant people; **does not** exclude Jewish people from people of God; “dogs” = those who refuse full covenant membership of Gentile believers; co-opts into Abrahamic covenant circumcision symbolizes.  
- Quote: “Paul’s bold claim that all believers in Christ are included in the circumcision… does not imply that the Jewish people are excluded from the people of God… Those dogs are those who refuse to recognize that Gentile believers in Christ have full covenant membership in the people of God.”  
- Locus: 3:3

**E71.** Hansen’s three characteristics of true circumcision: (1) serve/worship by Spirit; (2) boast in Christ Jesus; (3) put no confidence in flesh.  
- Quote: “(1) they serve God by his Spirit; (2) they boast in Christ Jesus; (3) they put no confidence in the flesh.”  
- Locus: 3:3

**E72.** Hansen: Spirit first as distinguishing mark/power (Gal 3–5 parallel), not primarily anti-opponent claim.  
- Quote: “we will gain a better understanding of this reference to the Spirit by rooting it in Paul’s own theology rather than by seeing it as a reaction to the position of his opponents.”  
- Locus: 3:3

**E73.** Hansen: “flesh” here = Jewish descent and circumcision ritual as ultimate security; national identity/ceremony rejected as **foundation** of relation to God (not bad in themselves).  
- Quote: “Confidence in the flesh gives ultimate significance to national identity and physical ceremony.” … “Although national identities and sacred ceremonies are not viewed as bad in themselves, they are rejected as the foundation for one’s relationship with God or with fellow believers.”  
- Locus: 3:3–4

**E74.** Hansen: shift to singular — Paul will beat Judaizers on their turf with superior résumé, then declare gains loss (v. 7); aim to **ridicule** status-in-flesh game and convince Philippians to reject Jewish-perfection propaganda.  
- Quote: “Paul’s ultimate aim is not to win this game of competition for status in the flesh but to ridicule those who value status in the flesh.”  
- Locus: 3:4

**E75.** Hansen résumé item 1: circumcised eighth day — “first class” vs proselyte circumcision; Gen 17:12; Lev 12:3.  
- Quote: “Even if the Gentile believers in Christ decided to reach for perfection within Judaism by getting circumcised, they would not be able to attain the perfection of a circumcision on the eighth day.”  
- Locus: 3:5

**E76.** Hansen item 2: *genos* Israel = ancestral stock/genealogical purity, not merely *laos*; Gentile proselytes cannot be of the “race.”  
- Quote: “Paul is claiming genealogical purity; his blood is untainted by any Gentile blood.”  
- Locus: 3:5

**E77.** Hansen item 3: tribe of Benjamin — noble ancestry (Josephus parallel); Benjamin traditions (Rachel, first king, loyalty to Judah, Jerusalem territory); Hebrew name Saul.  
- Quote: “so Paul appears to be proud that he belongs to the tribe of Benjamin.”  
- Locus: 3:5

**E78.** Hansen item 4: “Hebrew of Hebrews” = linguistic/cultural orientation vs Hellenized Jews; not mere mother tongue; still fluent Greek/rhetoric; “Palestinian vs Hellenistic” simple contrast inadequate; Dispersion does not equal Hellenized.  
- Quote: “By his claim to be a Hebrew of Hebrews, Paul clearly places himself on the side of those in Israel who ‘chose to die rather than to be defiled by food or to profane the holy covenant.’”  
- Locus: 3:5

**E79.** Hansen items 5–7 shift to personal achievements: Pharisee / zeal / faultless law-righteousness.  
- Quote: “The next three features display Paul’s own personal achievements: his membership in an elite group… nationalistic effort… and his perfection in his obedience to the law.”  
- Locus: 3:5–6

**E80.** Hansen on Pharisee: exact explication of laws; purity/Sabbath; name “separated ones”; law-centered/controlled/promoting; Philippians could never match that superiority.  
- Quote: “as a Pharisee his life was totally law-centered, law-controlled, and law-promoting.”  
- Locus: 3:5

**E81.** Hansen on zeal: Maccabean/Phinehas tradition of zeal for law; object of zeal is law (sandwiched between law phrases); Gal 1:13–14 parallel; nationalistic defense of purity, wider than later Zealot violence alone.  
- Quote: “Zeal was the code word in Paul’s time for ‘a fervent commitment to defending the purity of Israel’s religious practice and of her communal institutions, even at the cost of life itself.’”  
- Locus: 3:6

**E82.** Hansen: persecution of church = expression of zeal; Acts threats/imprisonment; defending law against crucified-Messiah worship; church as “new Israel” reading supported by 3:3 true circumcision; bitter irony — purifying Israel by persecuting true people of God; post-conversion = greatest sin / least of apostles (1 Cor 15:9–10).  
- Quote: “From the perspective of boasting about his Jewish achievements in the flesh, Paul could list his persecution of the church as uncontested evidence for his extreme zeal for the law. But from the perspective of his new life in Christ, his persecution of the church was viewed as the greatest of his sins…”  
- Locus: 3:6

**E83.** Hansen on “righteousness based on the law, faultless”: righteousness = upright behavior quality; Pharisaic oral-law perfection “without lapse or defect”; **faultless ≠ sinless** — “blameless observance… involved using the means of atonement for sin”; more than subjective clear conscience — objective, verifiable record.  
- Quote: “Within the framework of the entire law, however, faultless does not mean sinless, since ‘a blameless observance of the law involved using the means of atonement for sin.’” … “He is pointing to an objective feature of his portrait, as observable and verifiable as his circumcision and his persecution of the church.”  
- Locus: 3:6

**E84.** Hansen on tension with Gal 3 / Rom 5:20: not general principle of human ability to be faultless by law; **polemical ad hominem** to disarm law-promoters; then gains = loss (3:7) and contrast righteousness from God by faith (3:9).  
- Quote: “Paul is not presenting a general theological principle about human ability to be faultless by observing the law. His argument is designed to disarm the promoters of the law by boasting that he has more reasons than they do for confidence in the flesh.”  
- Locus: 3:6

**E85.** Hansen universalizes briefly: national pride and performance trophies eclipse Christ in every age; ultimately only Christ matters.  
- Quote: “No matter how precious the social privileges and how perfect the moral accomplishments may be, all that ultimately, eternally matters for a follower of Christ is Christ.”  
- Locus: end 3:4–6

---

### B. Losing All to Know Christ (3:7–11)

**E86.** Lemma 3:7–11: gains → loss for Christ; everything loss for surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord; lost all things; garbage to gain Christ and be found in him; not own righteousness from law but through faith in Christ — righteousness from God on basis of faith; know Christ — power of resurrection and participation in sufferings, becoming like him in death; somehow attaining resurrection from the dead.  
- Locus: 3:7–11 lemma

**E87.** Hansen: second self-portrait juxtaposed to 3:4–6; faultless law-righteousness worthless vs righteousness from God; **theological outline**: justification v. 9; sanctification v. 10; glorification v. 11.  
- Quote: “As he describes his own personal experience of new life in Christ, Paul provides a theological outline of the entire scope of salvation in Christ: justification… (v. 9); sanctification… (v. 10); and glorification… (v. 11).”  
- Locus: 3:7–11 intro

**E88.** Hansen: nine references to Christ in five verses; conversion not labeled but “profound reorientation”; remains Jew affirming Abraham’s God and Scriptures yet transformed by ambition to know crucified/risen Christ.  
- Quote: “True, Paul always remained a Jew who believed in the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and affirmed the divine authority of the Hebrew scriptures, but he was radically transformed by his supreme ambition to know the crucified, risen Christ and to become like him (3:10).”  
- Locus: 3:7–11 intro

**E89.** Hansen five parallels Paul//Christ hymn (2:5–11): consider privileges loss // not exploit equality; give up all to be found in Christ // made nothing / found as human; conformed to death // servant form, obedient to death; know Christ as Lord // universal confession Lord; resurrection power / attain resurrection / body like glorious body (3:21).  
- Quote: “Paul carefully crafts the story of his transformation to convince his readers that his choice to renounce his confidence in the flesh is the choice they too must make in order to know Christ and be conformed to Christ in his humiliation and exaltation.”  
- Locus: 3:7–11 intro

**E90.** Hansen: parallel also marks infinite difference — Christ *my Lord*; worship/obedience due only to God; depiction of incomparability leads to conclusion Christ is God though phrase “Christ is God” not literal.  
- Quote: “This confession is so strong that though Paul does not literally use the words ‘Christ is God,’ his depiction of the utter incomparability of Christ can lead to no other conclusion.”  
- Locus: 3:7–11 intro

**E91.** Hansen 3:7: “whatever were gains” = accounting terms, plural assets on balance sheet; now singular “loss” — not graduated discounts but **one huge liability** for sake of Christ.  
- Quote: “The shift from plural gains to singular loss indicates that Paul is not giving different values to each of his assets… Because of Christ, Paul has added up all of his assets and considered them to be one huge liability.”  
- Locus: 3:7

**E92.** Hansen: revaluation via “intellectual process”; conversion illuminates reason, not escape from reason.  
- Quote: “His conversion was not an escape from reason but an illumination of reason.”  
- Locus: 3:7

**E93.** Hansen 3:8: five conjunctions intensify expansion; perfect → present “I consider” = daily reaffirmation; object expands from “these things” (vv. 5–6) to **everything** competing for allegiance / encouraging confidence in flesh.  
- Quote: “in the context, everything refers to all things that encourage confidence in the flesh.”  
- Locus: 3:8

**E94.** Hansen: “surpassing worth of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord” — knowing = personal acquaintance via revelation and acknowledgment as Lord; insight + love; deepens OT knowledge of God (Jer, Hos).  
- Quote: “This knowledge is above all the ‘personal acquaintance’ of Christ Jesus.”  
- Locus: 3:8

**E95.** Hansen: “I have lost all things” = aorist focus on conversion renunciation; not theoretical; exclusion from Jewish community security used to thwart Judaizers’ offer of advantages.  
- Quote: “He presents his own experience of suffering for his faith in Christ to thwart any attempt on the part of the Judaizers to offer the Philippian Christians the advantages of belonging to the Jewish community.”  
- Locus: 3:8

**E96.** Hansen on *skybala* “garbage”: excrement/manure/kitchen scraps; vulgar term for totality of renunciation; renounces **goodness of the flesh**, not merely wickedness — goodness must not lurk beside Christ.  
- Quote: “What Paul renounced was not the wickedness of the flesh but all the goodness of his flesh. ‘That goodness is over and done with and abides under judgment; [it] must not have any form of lurking place alongside of Christ.’”  
- Locus: 3:8

**E97.** Hansen 3:9: chiasm gain Christ // be found in him; *heurethō* parallel to Christ “found” in human appearance (2:6–8); God’s assessment via righteousness from God; present and future coalesce.  
- Quote: “just as Christ was found to be in human form, Paul desires to be found in Christ.”  
- Locus: 3:9

**E98.** Hansen: renounced righteousness = “my own” (emphatic) + “from the law” = earned by obedience; repeats 3:6 faultless boast; viewed as loss/garbage; cf. Isa 64:6 filthy rags.  
- Quote: “He claims it to be my own righteousness because he had achieved it by keeping the law. He owned it because he had earned it.”  
- Locus: 3:9

**E99.** Hansen engages **New Perspective**: Sanders — “my righteousness” not merit of good deeds but result of being observant Jew / covenant membership; Dunn — not “achieved by me” but Israel’s covenant righteousness defended; Wright — covenant status by birth, circumcision badge, zealous Pharisee inner circle, not moralistic self-help.  
- Quote (Wright via Hansen): “That which he is refusing in the first half of verse 9 is not a moralistic or self-help righteousness, but the status of orthodox Jewish covenant membership.”  
- Locus: 3:9

**E100.** Hansen **partially accepts** NPP clarification (rejection of exclusivist only-circumcised-Jews-have-righteousness) but **rejects reduction** to national membership only: Kim’s challenge — if only national, why not “our own righteousness”?; Paul’s “I have more” (v. 4) rests on personal faultless achievement; zealous pursuit led to persecuting church; not “in and of itself a good thing.”  
- Quote: “Paul’s ‘own’ righteousness is the result of his personal zeal in fulfilling the law’s demands.” … “Thus, Paul’s reason for superior confidence in the flesh is not merely based on his national status but also on his personal achievement.”  
- Locus: 3:9 (also Gathercole footnote noted by Hansen)

**E101.** Hansen: two meanings of “righteousness” in contrast — own upright behavior from law vs gift/judicial right standing from God; gift opens union with Christ and inclusion open to all through faith, not only law-faultless.  
- Quote: “The righteousness from the law refers to Paul’s obedience to the law; the righteousness from God refers to a right relationship granted by God, not on the basis of obedience to the law, but on the basis of faith in Christ.”  
- Locus: 3:9

**E102.** Hansen on *pisteōs Christou* (**pistis Christou** debate): subjective genitive (“faithfulness of Christ”) has recent weighty defenders; Hansen holds **traditional objective genitive** “faith in Christ” on Philippians-internal evidence: faith/believe elsewhere (1:25, 27; 2:17; 1:29) of Philippians; 1:29 believe + suffer // 3:9–10 faith + sufferings; faith granted by God (not human virtue/work); double “faith” in 3:9 (means + basis; article anaphoric) stresses dependence on Christ vs law achievement.  
- Quote: “Although many recent interpreters present weighty arguments in favor of the view that this phrase means ‘the faithfulness of Christ,’ the traditional understanding of the phrase as a reference to faith in Christ still rests on solid evidence.”  
- Locus: 3:9

**E103.** Hansen 3:10: knowing Christ = power of his resurrection **and** participation (*koinōnia*) in his sufferings (one article = single entity); contemporaneous — resurrection power known in present sufferings; also future dimension via parallelism to v. 11.  
- Quote: “It is impossible to know the power of his resurrection without participation in his sufferings.”  
- Locus: 3:10

**E104.** Hansen: ABBA structure — power of resurrection / participation in sufferings // becoming like him in death / attaining resurrection from dead; full manifestation of resurrection power at 3:20–21 body transformation.  
- Quote: “This parallelism indicates that the knowledge of the power of Christ’s resurrection will be given in the future time concurrent with the resurrection from the dead.”  
- Locus: 3:10–11 (forward ref to 3:20–21)

**E105.** Hansen: power of resurrection ultimately **God’s** power (raised Christ; *dynamis* of God in gospel/cross/Spirit); contrasts former attempt to experience God’s power via law.  
- Quote: “In contrast to all his attempts to experience the power of God through strict observance of the law, Paul now knows the power of God by knowing Christ and the power of his resurrection.”  
- Locus: 3:10

**E106.** Hansen on *koinōnia* in sufferings: intentional reenactment/extension of Christ’s narrative, not mere psychological reframing; chosen relationship; places gospel partnership (1:5) within Spirit communion (2:1) and sufferings (3:10); **communal**, not individualistic martyr-only; genitive objective = objects shared; plural sufferings = range of afflictions (chains, struggles, Philippians’ suffering); primarily outward though linked to inward union.  
- Quote: “Paul speaks as one who intentionally participated in the narrative of Christ so that his story was a genuine reenactment and a purposeful extension of the narrative of Christ.” … “This participation in the sufferings of Christ cannot happen in isolation from others.”  
- Locus: 3:10

**E107.** Hansen: “becoming like him in his death” / being conformed (*symmorphizomenos*) — result of sufferings; *morphē* root echoes Christ hymn form of God/servant; three readings not exclusive: (1) martyrdom trajectory; (2) dying to sin / baptismal union (Rom 6) but not limited to beginning; (3) obedience in gospel proclamation conforming to obedient-unto-death.  
- Quote: “These three interpretations do not need to be set against each other as separate alternatives.”  
- Locus: 3:10

**E108.** Hansen 3:11: hope of resurrection from the dead; *exanastasis* + *ek nekrōn* emphasize future bodily rising from among the dead, not only present “to live is Christ”; futurity combats perfectionists claiming complete perfection now (**bridge toward 3:12**, not full 3:12 exposition).  
- Quote: “His emphasis on the futurity of resurrection from the dead is yet another way of combating the false teaching of perfectionists who are claiming their attainment of complete perfection in the present.”  
- Locus: 3:11

**E109.** Hansen on “somehow” (*ei pōs*): humility/self-distrust (cf. 1 Cor 9:27), not doubt of resurrection’s reality (cf. 3:21 confidence); avoids prideful claim of having earned resurrection.  
- Quote: “Although Paul has no doubt about the reality of the future resurrection from the dead… he does express an attitude of humility when he contemplates his own personal participation in this awesome future event.”  
- Locus: 3:11

**E110.** Hansen closing paren for unit: no rival power (Rome or Jewish religion) matches power that raises the dead; know exalted Christ → turn from earthly attractions.  
- Quote: “No other power - neither the power of the Roman Empire nor the power of the Jewish religion - can compete with the power that can raise the dead.”  
- Locus: end of 3:11 section in slice

## Absences / flags

1. **3:12+ main text not in this digest’s body exposition** — only anticipatory links (perfectionism; 3:17–21; 3:20–21). Slice F owns 3:12ff.
2. **Fragrant offering (4:18)** appears only as Hansen’s cross-reference while explaining 2:30 *leitourgia*/gifts — not a full 4:18 exegesis here.
3. **Footnote bodies** not reconstructed; only what Hansen states in continuous prose or short parenthetical scholarly attributions (Beare, Sanders, Dunn, Wright, Kim, Gathercole).
4. **Timothy “will be sent soon”** affirmed with delay-until-things-clear and “at once” after; Hansen does not invent trial outcome.
5. **Epaphroditus gambling etymology** explicitly rejected by Hansen.
6. **Interpolation of ch. 3** rejected; hesitation formula + positive/negative structure used as unity arguments.
7. **NPP on “blameless”/covenantal nomism**: Hansen accepts social Jew/Gentile stakes and atonement-means reading of “faultless ≠ sinless,” but insists personal achievement (not only national covenant status) is in view in 3:4–9; opposes reducing 3:9a to membership language alone.
8. **pistis Christou**: Hansen argues objective genitive for Philippians 3:9.
